name: Server Monitor
description: A status board of servers fed by reported check results, with check history and uptime
backend_requirements: Access control: anyone may read servers and their check history; require auth for registering, updating and deleting servers and for reporting check results; admin endpoints are restricted to the admin account
The app is a status board: check results are reported to it through POST /api/servers/:id/checks (by a monitoring script or a person), and the app itself never connects to the registered hosts
Servers: any signed-in user may register, update and delete any server; DELETE /api/servers/:id removes the server and its check history permanently
Server validation: name is a required non-empty string of at most 100 characters; host a required host name or IP address of at most 255 characters, without scheme, port or path

Checks: a check result has status online or offline and an optional response_ms (a whole number of at least 0); recording one sets the server's status and last_check from it, and a server without checks has status unknown and last_check null
Every server in a response carries uptime_percent: the share of its last 100 checks that were online, as a percentage rounded to one decimal, or null without checks
GET /api/servers lists active servers sorted by name; ?status= keeps servers with that current status (online, offline or unknown)
GET /api/servers/:id/checks lists a server's checks newest first; ?limit= caps how many are returned (default 50, at most 500) while total counts all of the server's checks
Deactivated servers (is_active false) are left out of GET /api/servers, answer 404 on the public server endpoints and accept no check results; the admin overview still lists them
Errors answer with a JSON object {"detail": "<message>"}: 400 for invalid input, 401 without a valid token, 403 for a non-admin on admin endpoints, 404 for unknown ids
frontend_requirements: Everyone sees the status board and server details read-only; signed-in users also get the add, edit, delete and report-check controls, and visitors see a 'Sign in to manage servers' prompt in their place
Sign-in and registration forms that call /api/auth/login and /api/auth/register; keep the token for later requests, show the signed-in username and offer sign-out

Status board: each server's name, host, a coloured status badge (online, offline, unknown), uptime and how long ago it was last checked, with a status filter; it refreshes every 30 seconds and has a manual refresh button
Server detail view: the server's fields and its recent checks (time, status, response time) as a table and a simple response-time chart
Add and edit server forms and a 'Report check' form (status and optional response time) that show the API's validation messages next to the form; delete asks for confirmation first
An empty state that explains how to register the first server when there are none
admin_requirements: Admin overview: every server, active or not, with total, active and inactive counts and the number of servers per current status
Toggle a server's active status from the overview

api_endpoints.description: List active servers by name with their current status

query.status: Only servers with this current status (online, offline or unknown)

api_endpoints.description: Replace a server's name and host (both required; status and history are kept)
Delete a server and its check history
Check results of a server, newest first

query.limit: How many of the newest checks to return (default 50, at most 500)

api_endpoints.description: Report a check result and update the server's status

data_models.name: Server
data_models.description: A monitored server; status and last_check mirror its newest check, uptime_percent is computed

fields.name: string (required, max 100 chars)
fields.host: string (required, host name or IP address, max 255 chars)
fields.status: string (one of: online, offline, unknown; unknown until the first check)
fields.last_check: datetime (null until the first check, ISO 8601 in JSON)
fields.is_active: boolean (default true; false hides the server from public endpoints)

fields.server_id: integer (references Server.id; deleted with the server)

admin_api_endpoints.description: Admin overview: every server with counts
